title: asterix: adjust to upstream change
description:
Structure change in asterix-specs, revision 3ab3bb3.
Rule type is generalized and it now also includes a default value.

notes.body:
Hi @zoranbosnjak, clang-tidy found the following:

```
/builds/wireshark/wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-asterix.c:55743:12: warning: function 'dissect_asterix_fields' is within a recursive call chain [misc-no-recursion]
 55743 | static int dissect_asterix_fields (tvbuff_t *tvb, packet_info *pinfo, unsigned offset, proto_tree *tree, uint8_t category, const AsterixField *current_uap[])
       |            ^
/builds/wireshark/wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-asterix.c:55743:12: note: example recursive call chain, starting from function 'dissect_asterix_fields'
/builds/wireshark/wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-asterix.c:55766:21: note: Frame #1: function 'dissect_asterix_fields' calls function 'dissect_asterix_fields' here:
 55766 |                     dissect_asterix_fields (tvb, pinfo, offset + start, asterix_field_tree, category, (const AsterixField **)current_uap[i]->field);
       |                     ^
/builds/wireshark/wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-asterix.c:55766:21: note: ... which was the starting point of the recursive call chain; there may be other cycles
/builds/wireshark/wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-asterix.c:55936:12: warning: function 'asterix_field_length' is within a recursive call chain [misc-no-recursion]
 55936 | static int asterix_field_length (tvbuff_t *tvb, unsigned offset, const AsterixField *field)
       |            ^
/builds/wireshark/wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-asterix.c:55936:12: note: example recursive call chain, starting from function 'asterix_field_length'
/builds/wireshark/wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-asterix.c:55967:29: note: Frame #1: function 'asterix_field_length' calls function 'asterix_field_length' here:
 55967 |                     size += asterix_field_length (tvb, offset + size, field->field[i]);
       |                             ^
/builds/wireshark/wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-asterix.c:55967:29: note: ... which was the starting point of the recursive call chain; there may be other cycles
```

Can you take a look? I added a couple of recursion checking routines (`increment_dissection_depth` and `decrement_dissection_depth`) earlier today in case they're useful here.

Hi @geraldcombs , not sure if I understand correctly.
Is there a problem which some particular recursive calls or the presence of the recursion is already a problem?

If someone can create traffic on the wire or in a capture file that causes uncontrolled recursion in a dissector, then that's a problem. In this case it looks like

- Our offset always advances when `dissect_asterix_fields` and `asterix_field_length` call themselves, and
- We're always guaranteed to be running over UDP.

If you can verify that both of those are the case then we can just add [Clang-tidy suppressions](https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/#id3). If ASTERIX might someday be extended to run over a streaming protocol, then we'll want to add recursion guards.

I understand the problem now.

Regarding the first bullet (the offset always advances)... it looks like this is the case for both functions. I have checked the cases when a function calls itself directly. Both functions are called recursively only once and in each case, the offset is advanced and so, the recursion will terminate eventually. It might be a good idea to rewrite the code such that this claim is more obvious or even to proove this to the the linter (if there is some way to do this). The problem remains for more complex loops or not direct calls, like: func1 -> calls func2 ... which calls back to func1.
This dissector will need some rewriting for other reasons and I will need some support when I come to this. So we might address this problem at the same time.

Regarding the second bullet (streaming)..., I don't think there will ever be a problem here. Asterix is always (even if streamed) processed in chunks (datablocks). First level of asterix is always in the form:
- category number (1 byte)
- total datablock length (2 bytes)
- actual data (different categories have different schema)
The recursive case becomes relevant only on the second level on the finite data.
Thanks for looking into this. I'm hoping to switch the Clang-tidy warnings to errors at some point so I added suppressions in !14718.
